correctness.rationale: The verifier independently generates radius-two unidirectional error balls and the classical distance d_u on all 128 binary length-seven words, checks their equivalence on every pair, constructs the 2976-edge compatibility graph, enumerates exactly 1680 four-cliques, and verifies that every four-clique has empty common-neighbor set. This proves maximum size four and exhausts all equality cases. It then recomputes both orbit classes, weight profiles, directional pair profiles, coverage counts and stabilizers. The classical optimum is also independently supported by Weber--de Vroedt--Boekee, Theorem 10(c), specialized to t=2.

value.rationale: For two unidirectional errors, n=7 is the first point in the classical exact small-length theorem where the optimum rises from two to four. Classifying every equality case at this threshold is a natural finite extremal problem. The two orbit types have different weight distributions and cover 72 versus 80 possible received words, so the classification exposes structural distinctions invisible in the known optimum cardinality.
